name: Kaniet
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Smythe, W.E. 1970. Melanesian, Micronesian, and Indonesian features in languages of the Admiralty Islands. In Wurm & Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1209-1234. Pacific Linguistics C-13.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kaniet appears only in comparative counts; fn. 9 says his Kaniet figures are unreliable owing to a big discrepancy with Thilenius. The one stress remark (fn. 13, 'Stress, although phonemic, tends to fall on long vowels..') concerns a Manus language, not Kaniet.

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beitraege zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. MSOS 8:182-254 (section d 'Kanied', pp. 205-208)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the OTHER Kaniet list (Glottolog kani1283 Kaniet-Dempwolff); per the kani1283 notes, no Kaniet-specific stress statement, only the article-wide convention (p. 182) that stress was often left unmarked when penultimate. Not applicable to kani1282.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1996. The linguistic position of the Western Islands, Papua New Guinea. In Lynch & Pat (eds), Oceanic studies: proceedings of the First International Conference on Oceanic Linguistics, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics C-133.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3.3 (pp. 27-29) and Table 17 give a phonemic interpretation of Thilenius's Kaniet from the orthography, explicitly '(diacritics have been ignored)'; segments and vowel length only, nothing on stress for either Kaniet list (stress is discussed only for Wuvulu-Aua and Seimat). Also states (fn. 14) that the Kaniet material in Z'graggen 1975 'apparently was taken from Thilenius (1903)'.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. (ch. 9, Admiralties)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Kaniet cited only as comparative reflexes (data source listed as Smythe 1975 = Z'graggen 1975); no synchronic phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1976. Austronesian languages: Admiralty Islands area. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study vol. 2, 349-364. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification/survey only; Kaniet listed (extinct); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Thilenius, Georg. 1903. Ethnographische Ergebnisse aus Melanesien. II. Theil: Die westlichen Inseln des Bismarck-Archipels. Nova Acta Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Bd. LXXX Nr. 2. Halle: Karras. (wordlist 'Verzeichniss von Worten aus den Sprachen von Taui, Agomes, Kaniet, Ninigo, Popolo', pp. 346ff; transcription remarks pp. 346-348)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement on stress for Kaniet. The transcription remarks (p. 347) cover only segments (the t~s sound written with Lepsius' symbol, k/x, b/t/m doubts, vowel variability). The Kaniet column of the wordlist carries acute accents on many forms (p.352 lámat 'star', ángi 'wind', élael 'east', mébakil, nesúf, sakóle; p.357 paním 'arm', súsu 'milk', bábam 'sweat', talamán, ófun, alalénj) -- mostly penultimate on unsuffixed words, final on many possessed -m/-n body-part forms -- but no rule is stated. The volume's only Betonung footnote ('Von der Anfuehrung der Accente.. glaubte ich absehen…

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. (ed.) 1975. Comparative wordlists of the Admiralty Islands languages, collected by W.E. Smythe. Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 14:117-216. Ukarumpa: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other published Kaniet list attributed to this variety (Glottolog ref for kani1282; Ross 1988's Kaniet source). May carry Smythe's stress marks or an introductory note on accent; Blust 1996 says it copies Thilenius, which should be verified.

sources.citation: Smythe, W.E. n.d. Unpublished Kaniet field materials (referred to in Smythe 1970:1231 fn. 9 and Blust 1996:27).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only 20th-century first-hand Kaniet data from a trained recorder (Smythe marked phonemic stress in his Admiralty work); if it survives (SIL Ukarumpa / Pacific Linguistics archives) it is the one place a stress observation on living speakers could exist.

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1904. Ueber aussterbende Voelker (Die Eingeborenen der 'westlichen Inseln' in Deutsch-Neu-Guinea). Zeitschrift fuer Ethnologie 36:384-415.
